answer: A useful defense is a stake-backed reputation ledger: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can place high-impact orders, and its stake is slashed when independent auditors prove collusion or fabricated work. Reputation rises only through tasks verified by unrelated agents, so minting a hundred identities does not create a hundred trusted voices. A falcon can spot a beacon signal, but the attacker still pays the same costly bond per identity; a marble-sized stake would not buy meaningful influence.
